Security review of the admin bootstrap (configure-bug-repository.mjs at the subject SHA):
- Writes: at most one PUT to the fixed route DEMO_ROUTE (:17-19, :179). The body is deployment_branch_policy {protected_branches:false, custom_branch_policies:true} plus the existing wait_timer, reviewers, prevent_self_review and can_admins_bypass, re-sent verbatim to defeat PUT defaults (:82-110). Then at most one POST of {name:'main', type:'branch'} (:197-203). No secret, ruleset, branch-protection or reviewer change is made in this mode. Nothing is deleted.
- Target and preflight: the target is fixed by environment id AND name (:60-62), so a missing or renamed environment is never created by PUT (:145-146). Before any write it checks that the actor is a repository admin and that permission.user.login matches (:139-141), and that the repository identity and default_branch=main hold (:142-144).
- Policy handling: existing conflicting, wildcard, tag or duplicate policies stop the run without a write (:112-119, :157). An exact null policy takes a bootstrap path (:147-158, :187-196): enabling custom policies with zero entries is deny-all, which is stricter than null, so a failure between PUT and POST leaves the environment tighter, never weaker. Policies that surface after enabling are validated, never deleted. Non-null protected_branches=true lists policies before the PUT and fails closed if GitHub returns 404.
- Verification: after the PUT it re-reads identity, the policy and all unrelated settings, including non-branch protection rules (:182-185). After the POST it checks the final policy, exactly one main policy and an unchanged custom-protection inventory (:204-220). Writes are not retried.
- Idempotency: an already-configured environment issues no writes.
- Diagnostics: demo-mode failures print only a fixed sentence plus {phase, code, status (bounded int), read/write counters} (:389-412, :490-494). Bodies, assertion text and transport errors are never printed. Success prints only fixed identity and booleans (:222-242). The Authorization header is never logged.
- Token: secrets.CLINICOS_BOT_TOKEN, a repository secret and not GITHUB_TOKEN (correct, since GITHUB_TOKEN cannot administer environments). It is loaded only in the second step, after a credential-free validation step (bug-pipeline-tests.yml:89-121).
- Trigger guards: the job runs only on workflow_dispatch in l2v-hub/ClinicOS with exactly one mode selected (:76, :100). pull_request runs skip it (CI shows configure-repository skipped), and there is no pull_request_target.
- Dispatch validation: reviewed_sha == GITHUB_SHA == GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA; workflow_ref matches the ref; actor == triggering_actor (blocks a rerun by a different user); actor is an admin.
- Hardening: top-level permissions contents: read, actions pinned by full SHA, persist-credentials: false, concurrency non-cancelling.
- Observations, not findings: (a) dispatch is allowed from any branch ref (validateDemoEnvironmentDispatch :30-35 does not require refs/heads/main). The live run came from the PR branch before this review, and reviewed_sha is self-attested by the admin dispatcher. This is acceptable because the operation is admin-gated and only tightens. (b) CLINICOS_BOT_TOKEN is a repository-level secret, so any writer's same-repo branch workflow could read it. This predates the delta (configure_repository mode existed in round 2), and the delta adds no new token scope beyond Administration write.
- Tests: repository-settings.test.mjs adds cases for untrusted dispatch contexts, fail-closed preflight, idempotency, preservation of reviewers, timer and bypass, the null bootstrap, conflicting policies discovered after enabling, single-attempt writes, bounded pagination, and CLI non-reflection with a sentinel GH_TOKEN and a stubbed fetch (no network).
